title: Reference mapping and batch-aware integration with ingest and BBKNN
repo_revision: ec37402 (abbreviated SHA shown for main; full SHA not exposed by inspected page)

sources.locator: “Integrating data using ingest and BBKNN”; PBMCs and Pancreas sections

scientific_use: Map cell labels and a reference embedding from an annotated reference dataset into query PBMCs, then compare asymmetric reference mapping with BBKNN batch-aware neighbor integration; the tutorial also applies BBKNN to a four-study human pancreas collection.
tool_role_basis: The workflow calls Scanpy ingest, PCA/neighbors/UMAP, and external BBKNN on observed single-cell expression datasets; it does not implement those algorithms.
inputs: AnnData reference and query matrices on intersecting genes, reference cluster labels and fitted PCA/neighbors/UMAP state; for pancreas, an already concatenated/intersected pancreas.h5ad with batch labels. Candidate bundled sources are PBMC processed and reduced datasets and the linked pancreas asset.
outputs: AnnData query with transferred labels and projected embedding; concatenated dataset with batch-aware neighbor graph and UMAP coordinates; visual comparison of label mapping and mixing. No persistent result artifact contract is specified beyond AnnData in-memory fields.
dependencies: Python, Scanpy, AnnData, UMAP dependencies; BBKNN external package; reference preprocessing and annotations. Tutorial environment snapshot identifies Scanpy 1.10.3 and AnnData 0.10.9 (historical notebook snapshot).
evidence: Tutorial explains reference PCA+neighbor-tree fitting and asymmetric label mapping; PBMC reference/query calls and intersected genes; pancreas source studies, download URL, and shape 14693×2448.
limitations: The tutorial does not provide a quantitative integration-quality grader; cell mixing visuals alone can hide biological overcorrection.
Pancreas preprocessing and batch metadata construction are not fully described in inspected excerpt; the linked Dropbox asset has not been downloaded or terms verified.
Ingest depends on a reference that captures relevant biology; tutorial explicitly notes reference size/coverage limits.
Task input, exact package versions, deterministic settings, and reference/query split require author decisions.

title: PAGA trajectory reconstruction of mouse hematopoiesis
repo_revision: ec37402 (abbreviated SHA shown for main; full SHA not exposed by inspected page)

sources.locator: “Trajectory inference for hematopoiesis in mouse”; preprocessing/visualization, optional denoising, PAGA and gene trends sections

scientific_use: Reconstruct myeloid and erythroid differentiation in Paul et al. mouse progenitor data using a graph abstraction over cell clusters, then inspect gene changes along selected PAGA paths; optional diffusion-map graph denoising and pseudotime are connected analyses.
tool_role_basis: The tutorial applies Scanpy preprocessing, graph, diffusion, PAGA and plotting methods to an existing biological dataset.
inputs: AnnData from scanpy.datasets.paul15 (2730 cells × 3451 genes; paul15_clusters labels and uns["iroot"] root metadata), followed by Zheng17 preprocessing; graph neighborhood configuration and chosen cell path/gene list for downstream expression trends.
outputs: PCA/diffusion representations, neighbor graph, graph layout, PAGA connectivity abstraction and path-based gene expression visualization/pseudotime-related artifacts stored in AnnData and plots.
dependencies: Scanpy, AnnData, NumPy/SciPy, graph layout and plotting dependencies; dataset loader; clustering labels and root-cell metadata. Notebook records Scanpy 1.10.3, AnnData 0.10.9.
evidence: Tutorial identifies Paul et al. 2015 differentiation question; loads paul15 and reports shape/metadata; calls recipe_zheng17, PCA, neighbors, draw_graph, optional diffmap; API docs list PAGA, DPT and graph methods.
limitations: The retrieved view was inspected through optional graph denoising but later gene-path sections were identified from table of contents, not fully examined.
Results rely on clustering resolution, graph settings and root/path selection; no external gold trajectory or executable grader is provided.
The bundled dataset loader provenance and original study accession/redistribution terms need verification before redistribution.
Exact task boundaries and deterministic outputs remain author decisions.

title: Quality control and highly variable gene selection with analytic Pearson residuals
repo_revision: ec37402 (abbreviated SHA shown for main; full SHA not exposed by inspected page)

sources.locator: “How to preprocess UMI count data with analytic Pearson residuals”; download, QC, variable-gene selection sections

scientific_use: Compare analytic Pearson-residual highly variable gene selection on two PBMC UMI count datasets and assess whether known cell-type markers rank among selected genes; tutorial also covers QC thresholds and residual preprocessing options.
tool_role_basis: Scanpy experimental preprocessing functions are applied to 10x count matrices, with known markers used as biological plausibility checks; no estimator is implemented in tutorial.
inputs: Raw filtered UMI count matrices in 10x Matrix Market directories for 3k PBMC v1 and 10k PBMC v3; gene symbols, per-cell counts/genes/mitochondrial fraction and a 12-gene marker list from the PBMC3k tutorial.
outputs: QC metrics and filtered AnnData matrices; Pearson-residual based ranking/selection of 2000 highly variable genes and diagnostic plots; residual transformed expression for downstream analyses.
dependencies: Scanpy experimental.pp, AnnData, pooch and tarfile for inputs, 10x Matrix Market reader, plotting stack; tutorial snapshot Scanpy 1.10.0 development build and older dependency versions. Chunking parameters matter for larger matrices.
evidence: Background states residual goals and relation to normalization/log transform; tutorial names two 10x PBMC inputs with URLs and SHA256s; defines QC filters, marker list, and selects n_top_genes=2000 with pearson_residuals flavor.
limitations: The notebooks’ marker inclusion check is a plausibility criterion, not an independent truth set or formal statistical validation.
QC thresholds differ between datasets and are inspired by another tutorial; dataset versions/chemistry affect comparability.
Tutorial is explicitly experimental API; version compatibility must be pinned.
Data archives were not downloaded, and redistribution/access terms were not checked.

title: Documented API for reference mapping and batch-balanced neighbors
repo_revision: ec37402 (abbreviated SHA shown for main; full SHA not exposed by inspected page)

sources.locator: PBMC mapping and BBKNN comparison sections

scientific_use: Provide a narrower task boundary to either map query labels/embeddings with ingest or construct a batch-balanced neighbor graph with BBKNN, preserving distinction between asymmetric transfer and joint graph integration.
tool_role_basis: Both are documented public/external API calls applied to AnnData, with tutorial-defined inputs and outputs.
inputs: ingest: reference with trained PCA, neighbor lookup, UMAP and categorical obs labels plus query sharing variables. BBKNN: concatenated AnnData with batch_key and PCA representation.
outputs: ingest adds transferred categorical annotations and embedding to query; BBKNN writes batch-balanced neighbor graph state used by UMAP or clustering.
dependencies: Scanpy, AnnData; UMAP for ingest; external bbknn package for BBKNN; prepared reference/query data or batch metadata.
evidence: Tutorial states ingest preserves data matrix and transfers labels/reference embedding; code intersects variables and calls ingest. It separately calls bbknn with batch_key on concatenated pancreas and PBMC data.
limitations: An API-level task requires authored acceptance criteria and quantitative evaluation; the docs provide qualitative plots.
BBKNN is an optional external dependency and current import/API version should be checked.

title: Pearson-residual preprocessing API for count matrices
repo_revision: ec37402 (abbreviated SHA shown for main; full SHA not exposed by inspected page)

sources.locator: Pearson residual background and highly variable gene selection

scientific_use: Normalize UMI counts under an analytic null model and select genes with excess residual variance as candidates for biological variability.
tool_role_basis: The operation invokes Scanpy’s experimental API on observed count matrices; method implementation is outside the unit.
inputs: Nonnegative UMI count matrix in AnnData; optional batch, clipping, chunk size and gene-selection settings; raw counts must be retained/selected as the working matrix.
outputs: Residualized expression matrix and/or highly-variable-gene flags/scores in AnnData; optionally a complete Pearson residual recipe output.
dependencies: Scanpy experimental module, AnnData, NumPy/SciPy; inputs must be raw counts; chunk size trades memory and speed.
evidence: Tutorial gives the statistical purpose of residuals, names APIs and shows flavor pearson_residuals with 2000 genes, plus chunk-size section.
limitations: Experimental API status and version pin need author review. No independent expected gene list is established beyond marker plausibility.
